importantNotes: Solomon's Temple was one of the most magnificent structures of the ancient world.
The kingdom split because Solomon turned to idolatry in his later years.
Elijah on Mount Carmel (ch. 18) is one of the most dramatic confrontations in the Bible.
God speaks to Elijah not in wind, earthquake, or fire, but in a still, small voice (19:12).
The divided kingdom pattern: 10 tribes (Israel/North) vs. 2 tribes (Judah/South).

chapters.1: David is old; Adonijah tries to seize the throne; Solomon is anointed king.
chapters.2: David's final instructions and death; Solomon establishes his kingdom.
chapters.3: Solomon asks God for wisdom; his wise judgment between two women.
chapters.4: Solomon's administration, prosperity, and fame for wisdom.
chapters.5: Solomon prepares to build the Temple with materials from King Hiram of Tyre.
chapters.6: The construction of Solomon's Temple in Jerusalem.
chapters.7: Solomon's palace complex and the Temple furnishings crafted by Huram.
chapters.8: The Ark is brought into the Temple; Solomon's prayer of dedication.
chapters.9: God appears to Solomon a second time; Solomon's other building projects.
chapters.10: The Queen of Sheba visits Solomon; his great wealth and splendor.
chapters.11: Solomon's foreign wives lead him to idolatry; God raises adversaries against him.
chapters.12: The kingdom divides — Rehoboam rules Judah, Jeroboam rules Israel.
chapters.13: A man of God prophesies against Jeroboam's altar; he is killed for disobedience.
chapters.14: Jeroboam's son dies; Rehoboam's reign; the Egyptian king Shishak invades Judah.
chapters.15: Kings of Judah (Abijah, Asa) and Israel (Nadab, Baasha).
chapters.16: Kings of Israel — Elah, Zimri, Omri, and the wicked Ahab who marries Jezebel.
chapters.17: Elijah prophesies drought; he is fed by ravens and raises a widow's son.
chapters.18: Elijah confronts the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel; fire falls from heaven.
chapters.19: Elijah flees from Jezebel; God speaks in a still, small voice; Elisha is called.
chapters.20: Ahab defeats Syria twice but disobeys God by sparing King Ben-Hadad.
chapters.21: Naboth's vineyard — Jezebel arranges Naboth's murder; Elijah pronounces judgment.
chapters.22: Ahab dies in battle against Syria as prophesied by Micaiah; Jehoshaphat rules Judah.
